Slow cook 2 lbs of boneless chicken thighs. With a mix of 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/2 brown sugar, 1/4 teaspoon ginger, 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes, 1/2 tbl spoon ketchup, 2 tbl spoons sesame seeds. The 2nd favorite is a instant new holiday meal. An actually good meatloaf. ½ cup packed brown sugar­ ½ cup ketchup (or sriracha sauce)­

1 lb ground beef­

1 lb ground turkey­

2 eggs­

1 ½ teaspoon salt

¼ teaspoon pepper

1 small onion, chopped (or ninja’d, depending on preference)­

¼ teaspoon ground ginger­

½ cup bread crumbs­

1 envelope dry onion soup mix­

4 ½ cups mashed potatoes (leftovers or pre­made work great. Wegman’s has some great pre­mades)

9 slices of cheese

Directions: 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Lightly grease a 5 x 9 loaf pan.

  1. Press the brown sugar into the bottom of pan and spread with ketchup/sriracha.

  2. Combine beef, turkey, and onions thoroughly.

  3. Mix in eggs, bread crumbs, dry soup mix, salt, pepper, and ginger.

  4. Layer as following until loaf is full: loaf mix, mashed potatoes, cheese slices.

  5. Bake for 1 hour (or slow cook for 3­6 hours)

Tabouli is a fairly easy thing to make and would be good for the summer.

¼ cup bulgur*

1 tsp salt

¼ cup lemon juice

2 cups parsley, washed, dried, and chopped

½ cup onion, finely diced

½ cup tomato, diced

¼ cup olive oil

Mix the bulgur and salt in a bowl. Then soak the mixture in the lemon juice. Let it sit for about 15 minutes, or until the juice is absorbed and the bulgur is tender. Add the other ingredients and mix. For extra credit, garnish with lemon slices.

*' In a pinch, you can use ground up wheat Chex instead of bulgur, but it will get soggy in a day or so. Bulgur has four different grinds – #2 Medium works best.

Butternut Squash & Chili Soup (this is a nice one)

Ingredients

1 Onion 1 Butternut Squash Birds eye chilies Ginger 1 tin of coconut milk stock cubes rice brown sugar 1 small tub of single cream (optional) butter Salt, pepper

Method

1 – Take an onion chop it up, and fry it in butter,

2 – Add 3 large chunks(or buy a good sized one and chop it up) of butternut squash to a large pot (Put the fried onion in there too),

3 – Put in 2 – 3 chopped birds eye chilies in the pot,

4 – Add about an inch of chopped fresh ginger,

5 – Add 1 tin of coconut milk and enough water to reach about 1 inch over the ingredients,

6 – Add 1 and 1⁄2 stock cubes and some salt,

6 – Add about 2 tablespoons of rice, cook the whole lot until it is all tender (cover and simmer basically),

7 – Add 2 -3 tablespoons of brown sugar to the pot, and maybe a small tub of single cream (if you fancy it),

8 – Use a hand blender to blitz the soup until it is smooth,

9 – Season to taste.
